title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and jailed for about six months after Fargo, North Dakota police falsely charged her with bank theft. She was held nearly four months in a Tennessee county jail awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota. The charges, four counts of unauthorized use of personal identifying information and four counts of theft, were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records showing she was in Tennessee at the time. She was released on Christmas Eve and learned she had lost her home, car, and personal property.

Lipps has filed a federal lawsuit seeking $10 million in damages against the city of Fargo and police detective Lucas Heck. The suit says police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a social media photo, based on a fake ID used by a suspect, and did not investigate further before requesting an arrest warrant. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. The lawsuit seeks accountability and aims to push police to use facial recognition technology more carefully.
